newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PLAINS FED CATTLE TRADE THIN AT $64 -FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PLAINS FED CATTLE TRADE THIN AT $64 -FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade near midday on Tuesday was slow, with thin sales at $64.00 per cwt reported, unchanged from light activity on Monday, feedlot sources in the central and southern Plains said.
About 500 head likely to grade select and choice sold in Kansas, sources there said. There were no reported sales in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area.
Other bids at $63.00 to $64.00 were passed by owners who priced cattle $65.00 to $66.00, they said.
Most owners were asking higher prices amid ideas that beef prices had stabilized, several sources said.
Perceptions that packers need to start buying cattle soon also lent optimisim among owners that fed cattle prices could trend higher this week, some sources said.
However, outlooks for firm prices were somewhat dimmed by opposing views that packers were well stocked with cattle and could wait a few more days before actively buying more.
Attempts to boost fed cattle prices also could be blunted if beef prices fail to rally.
Beef at midday Tuesday was quoted down $0.29 to up $0.04, with 182 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $102.89, down $0.29 from Monday.
